question: What are the minimum credits and marks required to progress from Year One to Year Two in an Integrated Masters programme according to this document?

question: What are the conditions for postgraduate research students to apply for GTA or GLA positions?
expected_answer: Postgraduate research students are eligible to apply for GTA/GLA posts except when they are in further completion or an extension to completion period. Research supervisors need to agree that progress is good and that students can apply or continue to apply for GTA roles and agree the number of hours to be worked.
follow_up_question: Are there any specific restrictions on the number of hours a postgraduate student can work as a GTA or GLA?
follow_up_expected_answer: Any restrictions on hours set out in the University’s Principal Regulations for Research Degrees, RCUK training grant or any other scholarship will apply.

question: Which specific referencing styles and versions can be used by departments and schools at the University of Essex?
expected_answer: Departments and Schools should select a single referencing style and version from a limited list maintained by Library and Cultural Services. The selection is optional for postgraduate research cohorts, but a broad approach to referencing education must still be embedded.
follow_up_question: Can you provide an example of one of the allowed referencing styles?
follow_up_expected_answer: Yes, examples include APA, MLA, or Chicago, but only specific versions from these are permitted.

question: What should students do if they wish to raise a complaint related to the provision of continuity for their course of study?
expected_answer: Students should deal with their complaints through the Student Concerns and Complaints Procedure.
follow_up_question: What are possible outcomes if a student's complaint is upheld under this procedure?
follow_up_expected_answer: Possible remedies for the student include an apology, explanation, and/or practical remedies wherever possible.

question: How many members of staff must be nominated by a department if they have more than 149 postgraduate research students for potential Independent Chairs?
expected_answer: If a department has more than 149 postgraduate research students (i.e. 150 or more), they must nominate 4 members of staff to be listed as potential Independent Chairs.
follow_up_question: What happens if a department has fewer than the minimum number of nominations required for their PGR student community?
follow_up_expected_answer: The Faculty Education Committee approves the list of potential Independent Chairs annually, so departments will be notified by the Postgraduate Research Education Team how many nominations they must put forward.

question: What does QAA define dual awards as in the policy document?
expected_answer: Dual awards are defined as two degree-awarding bodies jointly designing a course of study comprising a joint initial curriculum leading to two separate qualifications awarded individually by the two degree-awarding bodies.
follow_up_question: Which components are necessary for obtaining a joint award according to the document?
follow_up_expected_answer: All components must be successfully completed and lead to a single joint award.

question: How long can a Postgraduate Research Degree (PGR) student request compassionate leave under this policy?
expected_answer: The PGR student can request up to two weeks of compassionate leave, which is equivalent to 10 working days.
follow_up_question: What happens when a PGR student returns to their studies after taking compassionate leave?
follow_up_expected_answer: When the PGR student returns, the supervisor should discuss any additional support needs and make referrals to appropriate support services as needed.

question: What do Masters of Philosophy wear for academic dress?
expected_answer: Masters of Philosophy wear a black gown, similar to other Masters, a hood of full shape with the outside University red and fully lined with white inside, and a black mortar-board.
follow_up_question: How is the academic dress for Honorary Doctors different from PhDs?
follow_up_expected_answer: Honorary Doctors wear a University red gown with black cuffs and facings, while PhDs have maroon sleeves and a black bonnet.

question: What happens if a student's work is sponsored by a commercial organization?
expected_answer: In such cases, the University’s Research and Enterprise Office helps draw up a contractual agreement with the commercial organisation concerned which will cover any special intellectual property provisions.
follow_up_question: Who is responsible for drawing up the agreement in case of sponsorship by a commercial organization?
follow_up_expected_answer: The University’s Research and Enterprise Office helps draw up the agreement.

question: What is the minimum Year Mark required for a student to be eligible for a Term Abroad in an Essex Abroad course?
expected_answer: A minimum Year Mark of 50 in Year One must be achieved. If during Year One, you undertook reassessment, the Uncapped Year Mark will be used.
follow_up_question: What happens if a student does not meet this requirement for the Term Abroad?
follow_up_expected_answer: The document does not specify what happens if a student does not meet the minimum Year Mark requirement.

question: What is the minimum Year Mark required for a student to be eligible for a Term Abroad under the Essex Abroad rules in the academic year 2025-26?
expected_answer: To be eligible for a Term Abroad, students must achieve a minimum Year Mark of 50 in Year One. If they undertook reassessment during Year One, the Uncapped Year Mark will be used to determine eligibility.
follow_up_question: What happens if a student fails to meet the minimum Year Mark requirement for a Term Abroad?
follow_up_expected_answer: Students who do not meet the minimum Year Mark of 50 in Year One will not be eligible for a Term Abroad. They must achieve the required mark before applying.

question: What is the minimum Year Mark required for a student to be eligible for a Term Abroad in Joint courses involving Modern Language/Language Studies at University of Essex?
expected_answer: A minimum Year Mark of 50 in Year One is required to be eligible for a Term Abroad.
follow_up_question: What happens if during Year One, a student undertakes reassessment for Joint courses involving Modern Language/Language Studies?
follow_up_expected_answer: If during Year One, the student undertakes reassessment, the Uncapped Year Mark will be used to determine eligibility for a Term Abroad.

question: What is the pass mark for all modules of the Graduate Diploma according to these rules?
expected_answer: The pass mark for all modules of the Graduate Diploma is 40.
follow_up_question: How are credits rounded in cases where a student scores exactly halfway between two whole numbers?
follow_up_expected_answer: For the purposes of these rules, taught module averages and the overall weighted average for the taught module will be rounded to the nearest whole number – i.e. 39.5 will count as 40, 39.4 as 39.

question: What are the specific requirements for a student to achieve a Distinction in Year One under the rules stated in this document?
expected_answer: To achieve a Distinction in Year One, a student must have either: (a) A Year Mark of 70 or above; or (b) 60 Credits at 70 or above with a Year Mark of 68 or 69.
follow_up_question: What happens if a student does not meet the requirements to progress from Year One under these rules?
follow_up_expected_answer: If a student does not meet the progression requirements, they will be considered for transfer to an Honours Degree programme or must undertake necessary reassessment prior to the next academic year.

question: What are the requirements for a student to achieve a Distinction in Year One of the Integrated Masters programme in Modern Languages (Translation)?
expected_answer: To achieve a Distinction, students must have either: A Year Mark of 70 or above; or 60 Credits at 70 or above with a Year Mark of 68 or 69.
follow_up_question: What happens if a student fails to meet the requirements for progression but has passed more than 30 credits in Year One?
follow_up_expected_answer: Students must undertake necessary reassessment prior to the next Academic Year in order to fulfil the requirement to progress. Marks will be capped at 40.

question: What is the maximum number of non-core credits that can be failed in Year One and still pass to the Final Year under the University of Essex Foundation Degree rules?
expected_answer: You can fail a maximum of 15 non-core credits across your degree, so if you fail 15 non-core credits in Year One, you cannot fail any more credits in your degree.
follow_up_question: What happens if a student fails more than 15 non-core credits in Year One?
follow_up_expected_answer: If a student fails more than 15 non-core credits in Year One, they will not be able to continue their studies under the University of Essex Foundation Degree rules.

question: What is the requirement for passing Year One according to the rules of assessment?
expected_answer: To pass Year One and proceed to Year Two, students must pass all modules and achieve 120 credits in the Year at Level 4.
follow_up_question: What happens if a student does not pass all modules but still meets the credit requirement?
follow_up_expected_answer: The specific rules for such scenarios are not detailed in this document, and the process may involve reassessment or other measures as outlined in subsequent sections.

question: What is the maximum number of non-core credits that can be condoned across a three-year Honours Degree at Essex University?
expected_answer: The maximum number of non-core credits that can be condoned across a Three-Year Honours Degree is 15.
follow_up_question: How are the failed non-core credits recorded if they are not condoned or trailed?
follow_up_expected_answer: Failed non-core credits that are neither condoned nor trailed will be recorded in the final year’s marks and affect the calculation of the final degree classification.

question: What are the consequences for students who fail to complete the required placement hours in EG124, EG226, or EG229 modules?
expected_answer: If a student fails to complete the required placement hours by the end of Week 36, they will receive a FAIL for this element and cannot undertake the Professional Performance Assessment. They may be offered reassessment in the next academic year if they have failed the placement element.
follow_up_question: What is the process for obtaining in-person reassessment for a student who has not completed their relevant placement hours?
follow_up_expected_answer: Except where there are accepted Extenuating Circumstances, in-person reassessment without attendance or trailing reassessment in the next Academic Year can only be offered where the student has completed their placement hours but have failed to achieve a Pass Mark of 40.

question: What is the minimum pass mark for modules in Year Four of the MSci Nursing programme?
expected_answer: The pass mark for modules in Year Four is 50.
follow_up_question: What happens if a student fails an assessment on their final attempt without valid extenuating circumstances?
follow_up_expected_answer: Students will be required to withdraw from the programme.

question: What is the pass mark required for the HS831 linguistics and phonetics exam, and how is it adjusted to reflect a standard pass mark of 50?
expected_answer: The pass mark required for the HS831 linguistics and phonetics exam is at least 74. The 74 examination pass mark will be adjusted proportionately to represent in real terms the mark students would achieve if the module used the standard pass mark of 50 that applies to other modules.
follow_up_question: How is the transformed grade calculated for students who achieve a raw grade below the adjusted pass mark in HS831?
follow_up_expected_answer: The transformed grade is achieved by applying the formula: Transformed grade = 1.92 x [raw grade – 74] + 50.

department: School of Sport, Rehabilitation and Exercise Science
question: What are the criteria for a student to receive credit from taught modules under these rules?
expected_answer: A core module must be taken as part of the programme structure and passed, with no condonement of marks below a pass allowed. Credits are only awarded if the module is passed.
follow_up_question: Which modules require students to achieve specific pass marks beyond the standard 50%?
follow_up_expected_answer: For HS632 Preparation for Independent and Supplementary Prescribing V300 (NMC/HCPC) Pharmacology Examination, a student must achieve a pass mark of 80. For SE708 (and the alternative SE746) the MCQ exam pass mark is 70%.

question: What are the credit limits for condonable non-core modules at each level?
expected_answer: The credit limits are as follows: The MRes limit is 60; the Masters is 40; the Postgraduate Diploma is 30; the Postgraduate Certificate is 20.
follow_up_question: How many credits must be passed to achieve a pass in the Masters degree according to the MRes Rules of Assessment?
follow_up_expected_answer: To be awarded a pass in the Masters, a student should attempt 360 credits at Masters Level (Level 7) of which 300 must be passed, with the remaining credits condoned, subject to (c).

question: What are the criteria for a student to be eligible for an award of a pass in the Graduate Certificate program?
expected_answer: To be awarded a pass in the GRADUATE CERTIFICATE, a student should obtain 60 credits; pass all the taught core modules; pass all assessments; and meet all the attendance requirements for the programme.
keyphrases: pass all the taught core modules
follow_up_question: What happens if a student fails a taught module in the Graduate Certificate program?
follow_up_expected_answer: Students who have failed any taught module may have a second attempt at the assessment for the module(s).

question: What are the progression requirements for students in Essex Business School's Integrated PhD program under Model A?
expected_answer: To pass Year One and proceed to Year Two of the Integrated PhD, a student must: attempt 180 credits at Masters level (level 7), pass all taught core modules with a mark of 60 or more, condone failure in up to 40 credits in non-core taught modules as long as the overall weighted average is 50 or above, pass the dissertation or equivalent with a mark of 65 or more, and achieve an overall weighted average mark of 65 or more for all taught modules and the dissertation.
keyphrases: pass all taught core modules with a mark of 60 or more
up to 40 credits in non-core taught modules
overall weighted average mark of 65 or more
follow_up_question: What happens if a student fails a core module but still meets the overall weighted average requirement?
follow_up_expected_answer: The student will be offered reassessment in the individual core module where they did not meet the progression requirements, and the marks achieved after reassessment will be used to determine eligibility to progress to Year Two of the Integrated PhD.

question: What criteria must be met to achieve a pass, merit, and distinction in the Masters degrees under these rules?
expected_answer: To achieve a pass, students need an overall weighted average of at least 50. For a Merit, they should have an overall weighted average mark of 60 or more. For a Distinction, they must have an overall weighted average mark of 70 or more.
follow_up_question: How are credits and marks handled when a student fails with a mark between 40-49.5?
follow_up_expected_answer: Failure with a mark of 40 or more for up to 40 credits in non-core taught modules may be condoned provided the overall weighted average for all the taught modules is 50.

question: What must be ensured by Heads of Department regarding student progress monitoring, as per the document?
expected_answer: Heads of Department are responsible for ensuring that an effective means of monitoring students' progress and attendance is established and maintained in each department.
follow_up_question: What should be communicated to all students by Heads of Department regarding their progress monitoring procedures?
follow_up_expected_answer: Departmental procedures, including norms for formal face-to-face meetings between students and their supervisor(s), should be communicated to all students in the Department.

question: What is the expected time frame for the return of assessed work according to the University's policy?
expected_answer: The expectation for the return of assessed work should be within 20 working days.
follow_up_question: What should departments do if they are unable to meet their stated deadline for providing feedback?
follow_up_expected_answer: Departments should inform students of this and advise them of the revised arrangements.

question: What is the submission deadline for candidates first registered from October 2018 onwards?
expected_answer: The submission deadline of the thesis for examination is at the end of the standard period of study.
follow_up_question: What happens if a candidate requires an extended completion period beyond the standard period?
follow_up_expected_answer: If deemed necessary by the Supervisory Panel and Research Students’ Progress Board, a one, two or three-term period of completion may be recommended to the relevant Faculty Dean for approval.

question: How long does a research degree viva last, and what happens if it runs long?
expected_answer: The length of a viva varies, but if it lasts longer than two hours the internal examiner or Independent Chair will recommend an adjournment for a break.
follow_up_question: Who normally attends the viva?
follow_up_expected_answer: The viva normally involves only the external examiner, the internal examiner (or second external examiner) and the candidate. The Faculty Dean (Postgraduate) may appoint an Independent Chair to oversee the conduct of the oral examination. The candidate's supervisor is not normally present and may attend only in exceptional circumstances, approved individually.
follow_up_keyphrases: supervisor will not normally be present

source_title: Policy for the Appointment of Independent Chairs for Research Degree Vivas
question: In which circumstances will the Faculty Dean Postgraduate appoint an Independent Chair for a viva?
expected_answer: An Independent Chair is appointed when: the Internal Examiner has no experience in research degree examining; the Internal Examiner is new to research degree examining at Essex and has not undertaken Internal Examiner training; the viva follows a referral and resubmission of a thesis; the viva follows an appeal; there are circumstances affecting the candidate that make it desirable; the candidate is a member of staff of the University or a Partner Institution being examined as a staff candidate; or where agreed in individual cases to be necessary.
keyphrases: no experience in research degree examining
follow_up_question: Who is eligible to be nominated, and can they come from the candidate's own department?
follow_up_expected_answer: A nominee must be a permanent member of staff who has been an Internal Examiner for at least two postgraduate research examinations at Essex, or has examined two theses externally and undertaken University of Essex Independent Chair training, and must have a good understanding of the University's procedures and regulations for the award being examined. The Independent Chair chosen will be from outside the candidate's department and will have no conflict of interest with the candidate, the supervisor or the External Examiner.
follow_up_keyphrases: at least two postgraduate research examinations

question: Who must a department designate to lead each professional doctorate at Essex, and who are they responsible to?
expected_answer: Each department must designate a Professional Doctorate Director for each professional doctorate, a group of professional doctorates or equivalent, who is an experienced doctoral student supervisor. The Director is responsible to the Head of Department for the departmental arrangements for the relevant PD students, and liaises with and reports as necessary to the Dean.
follow_up_question: Which Dean do professional doctorate decisions normally get referred to?
follow_up_expected_answer: In practice most decisions are referred to the Faculty Dean Postgraduate through the Postgraduate Research Education Team. 'Dean' refers to the Executive Dean (or their deputy) or the Dean of Partnerships (or their deputy).

source_title: Code of Practice: Professional Doctorates for the Tavistock and Portman NHS Foundation Trust 2025-26
question: For Tavistock and Portman professional doctorates, who is designated to lead each programme and who are they responsible to?
expected_answer: The Trust designates a Course Lead for each Professional Doctorate, a group of professional doctorates or equivalent, who is an experienced doctoral student supervisor. The Course Lead is responsible to the Portfolio Manager for the Trust arrangements for the relevant PD students.
follow_up_question: Which Dean do decisions get referred to for these programmes?
follow_up_expected_answer: For Tavistock and Portman professional doctorates, 'Dean' refers to the Dean of Partnerships (or their deputy), and most decisions are referred to the Dean of Partnerships through the Postgraduate Research Education Team.

source_title: Code of Practice: Professional Doctorates for the Tavistock and Portman NHS Foundation Trust 2025-26
question: Can a viva be waived for a professional doctorate, and who decides?
expected_answer: Permission to waive a viva on first submission will only be granted by the Dean in exceptional circumstances. The Postgraduate Research Education Team would then notify the student of the examiners' wish not to hold a viva and the reasons for it, and the student would be told they have the right to have a viva if they wish.
follow_up_question: What if the thesis has been referred?
follow_up_expected_answer: Where a thesis has been referred, the rules for waiving the viva on a referred thesis apply as set out in the Code of Practice, separately from the first-submission case.

question: A student has failed a core taught module with a mark of 45. Can that failure be condoned?
expected_answer: No. Condonement applies only to non-core modules - failure with a mark of 40 or more may be condoned for up to 20 credits in non-core modules. All taught core modules must be passed, so a failed core module cannot be condoned regardless of the mark.
follow_up_question: How many credits can be condoned in total?
follow_up_expected_answer: Failure with a mark of 40 or more may be condoned for up to 20 credits in non-core modules, provided the other progression requirements are met.

question: Both examiners have read the thesis and think the candidate is likely to be referred. They would rather not hold a viva. Can it be waived?
expected_answer: No. Vivas will not be waived where one or more examiners has deemed from reading the thesis that the candidate seems likely to fail, to only be eligible for a lower award, or to be referred.
follow_up_question: What happens to a candidate who will not engage with viva arrangements at all?
follow_up_expected_answer: A candidate who does not engage with the arrangements to the extent that it has not been possible to arrange a viva shall be deemed to have withdrawn permanently from the University and from their research degree, unless it has been agreed that the viva can be waived.

source_title: Code of Practice: Postgraduate Research Degrees
question: We would like a visiting academic to supervise one of our PGR students. Is that permitted?
expected_answer: Not as a supervisor in the normal sense - visiting staff cannot be appointed as a supervisor of a PGR student unless they are formally appointed via the associate supervisor route.
follow_up_question: Does the same restriction apply on professional doctorates?
follow_up_expected_answer: Yes. The Code of Practice for Professional Doctorates carries the same restriction: visiting staff cannot be appointed as a supervisor of a PGR student unless formally appointed via the associate supervisor route.

question: Can a professional doctorate student's standard period of study be shortened, and whose approval is needed?
expected_answer: Yes, but only in exceptional circumstances and with the Deans' approval. The standard period of study may be reduced in exceptional circumstances with the Deans' approval.
keyphrases: standard period of study may be reduced
follow_up_question: What is expected of a student entering a completion period?
follow_up_expected_answer: A student entering a completion period does so on the understanding that their full thesis will be ready for submission by the end of that completion period.

source_title: Code of Practice: Professional Doctorates for the Tavistock and Portman NHS Foundation Trust 2025-26
question: A referred thesis has come back and the examiners recommend a pass. Do we still need to hold a second viva?
expected_answer: Not necessarily. Where the recommendation on the referred thesis is a pass, a request by the examiners to waive the viva will normally be granted. Where the recommendation is not a pass, a waiver will only be granted in exceptional circumstances.
follow_up_question: And on first submission?
follow_up_expected_answer: On first submission, permission to waive a viva will only be granted by the Dean in exceptional circumstances. The Postgraduate Research Education Team would notify the student of the examiners' wish not to hold a viva and the reasons, and the student would be told they have the right to have a viva if they wish.

source_title: Code of Practice: Postgraduate Research Degrees
question: A Supervisory Panel wants to discontinue a student. Can the Panel make that decision itself?
expected_answer: No. A decision or recommendation for discontinuation, downgrading or upgrading, to confirm PhD status or change to MPhil, to permit entry into completion, or to extend the standard period can only be made by the RSPB. The Supervisory Panel can only recommend.
follow_up_question: Are there any restrictions on who sits on the RSPB for that decision?
follow_up_expected_answer: Yes. Where the RSPB is considering a recommendation of discontinuation or downgrading, or a change of status to MPhil at confirmation, the RSPB membership must include at least two members who were not on the student's last Supervisory Panel. Smaller departments may co-opt a supervisor from another department in a cognate discipline to satisfy this.
follow_up_keyphrases: at least two members who were not

question: Can the student's main supervisor chair their Supervisory Panel?
expected_answer: No. The chair must not be a partner or close relative of the supervisor (main, joint or secondary), and must not have a professional or personal relationship with the student that might give rise to a conflict of interest.
follow_up_question: What happens if a professional practice supervisor has to step down partway through?
follow_up_expected_answer: Where a professional practice supervisor cannot continue supervision for whatever reason, the department must ensure that a replacement supervisor is appointed.

question: A supervisor has asked to sit in on their student's viva. Is that allowed, and who decides?
expected_answer: Not normally. The candidate's supervisor will not normally be present at the viva and can only be present in exceptional circumstances, approved on an individual basis by the Faculty Dean (Postgraduate) and with the agreement of the examiners. It is good practice for the supervisor to be invited to attend at the end of the viva when the examiners communicate their recommendation.
follow_up_question: Can they be there when the outcome is given?
follow_up_expected_answer: Yes - it is good practice for the supervisor to be invited to attend at the end of the viva when the examiners communicate their recommendation to the candidate.

source_title: Code of Practice: Postgraduate Research Degrees
question: Our PGR student is sponsored under a Student visa. Can their supervision meetings be held over Zoom?
expected_answer: Only to a limited extent. For students with immigration sponsorship the majority of contact should be face-to-face; in exceptional circumstances the University may agree that contact can be via video link. Virtual meetings must not breach progress monitoring requirements for students subject to immigration control.
keyphrases: majority of contact should be face-to-face
follow_up_question: Is it different for Distance Learning students?
follow_up_expected_answer: Yes. There is no general requirement for Distance Learning students to attend face-to-face Supervisory Panels and they may have all Supervisory Panels held via Zoom if deemed more appropriate. If a department wishes to require face-to-face panels or other on-campus activity for a Distance Learning student, that must be specified when the details of the arrangement are set.

source_title: Code of Practice: Postgraduate Research Degrees
question: If a student is granted an extension, does that affect how much completion time they have left?
expected_answer: Yes. In such instances the subsequent number of completion periods available to the student will be reduced by one term, unless exceptional circumstances make that reduction inappropriate. Students must be offered an opportunity to discuss this with the RSPB before the final recommendation is forwarded to the Dean for approval.
follow_up_question: Can an extension of more than one term ever be granted?
follow_up_expected_answer: Yes - in exceptional circumstances an extension of more than one term may be granted.

question: A student resubmits an assessment for a module they had already passed overall. Can their module mark go up?
expected_answer: No. If the pre-resubmission module aggregate was above the pass mark, the resubmission cannot improve the module aggregate mark - the module aggregate is capped at the pre-resubmission aggregate.
follow_up_question: And if they had failed the module overall?
follow_up_expected_answer: If the pre-resubmission module aggregate was below the pass mark, the resubmission can improve the module aggregate mark up to the pass mark only.

question: Does an exit award have to carry the same title as the main programme?
expected_answer: Normally yes - the title of the exit award will be the same as for the main programme, unless a different title has been approved in order to meet Professional, Statutory or Regulatory Body requirements.
follow_up_question: Which awards does the credit framework actually cover?
follow_up_expected_answer: The Postgraduate Taught Programme Credit Framework covers Masters degrees, PG Diplomas, PG Certificates, and Integrated Masters degrees (Final Stage only).

source_title: Policy for the Appointment of Independent Chairs for Research Degree Vivas
question: Our department has 160 PGR students. How many Independent Chair nominations do we have to put forward?
expected_answer: Four. Departments with 150 or more PGR students must put forward 4 nominations (1-99 require 2, 100-149 require 3).
follow_up_question: Do departments without any PGR students have to nominate anyone?
follow_up_expected_answer: No - but they may if they wish. All departments are able to nominate Independent Chairs to be approved by the Faculty Education Committee, including those without PGR students if they wish.

source_title: Code of Practice: Professional Doctorates for the Tavistock and Portman NHS Foundation Trust 2025-26
question: For a Tavistock professional doctorate, who can decide to permit a student to enter their completion period?
expected_answer: Only the RSPB. A decision or recommendation for discontinuation or downgrading, to permit entry into completion, or to extend the standard period can only be made by the RSPB.
keyphrases: can only be made by the RSPB
follow_up_question: Who does the Course Lead report to for these programmes?
follow_up_expected_answer: The Course Lead is responsible to the Portfolio Manager for the Trust arrangements for the relevant PD students, and liaises with and reports as necessary to the Dean - which for these programmes is the Dean of Partnerships (or their deputy).
follow_up_keyphrases: Portfolio Manager for the Trust arrangements

question: A candidate keeps failing to respond about viva arrangements and we cannot get one scheduled. What is the position?
expected_answer: A candidate who does not engage in viva arrangements to the extent that it has not been possible to arrange a viva shall be deemed to have withdrawn permanently from the University and from their research degree, unless it has been agreed that the viva can be waived.
follow_up_question: What if they cannot engage because of exceptional circumstances?
follow_up_expected_answer: The Code provides for waiving the viva where there are exceptional circumstances which prevent a candidate from engaging in the viva process, so the withdrawal position would not apply in that case.

follow_up_question: Is there anything on the paperwork or approvals involved?

follow_up_question: Can you tell me how many there are in each department?

question: What are the pass marks for the Project Demonstration Oral and written Dissertation element in the MSc Applications of Artificial Intelligence programme?
expected_answer: Students must achieve a pass mark of 50 in both the Project Demonstration Oral (PDO) and the written Dissertation element to pass the module and achieve the credits.
follow_up_question: Are there any specific conditions or requirements for passing the MSc Applications of Artificial Intelligence programme other than the pass marks in the Project Demonstration Oral and written Dissertation element?
follow_up_expected_answer: No, the only requirement stated is that students must achieve a pass mark of 50 in both the Project Demonstration Oral (PDO) and the written Dissertation element to pass the module and achieve the credits.

question: What is the pass mark for the MSc Applications of Artificial Intelligence programme in the Project Demonstration Oral and written Dissertation element?
expected_answer: Students must achieve a pass mark of 50 in both the Project Demonstration Oral and the written Dissertation element to pass the module.
follow_up_question: What is the minimum requirement for passing the MSc Financial Technology (Computer Science) programme in terms of the Project Demonstration Oral and written Dissertation element?
follow_up_expected_answer: Students must achieve a pass mark of 50 in both the Project Demonstration Oral and the written Dissertation element to pass the module.

source_title: Policy on Compassionate Leave for Postgraduate Research Degree students
question: One of our PGR students has been bereaved. What leave can they take, and what happens if they need longer than that?
expected_answer: Compassionate leave can be sought for up to two weeks (10 working days), and the standard and maximum periods of study and the thesis submission date are automatically extended by the duration of the approved compassionate leave. If the longer-term impact requires a longer period of leave, the Policy on Leave of Absence (intermission) should be consulted instead - that is a separate policy with its own grounds and procedures.
follow_up_question: They may need longer than that, and they're part-time - does the part-time mode reduce what they can take?
follow_up_expected_answer: No. For longer leave the Policy on Leave of Absence (intermission) applies, and periods of intermission are not impacted or determined by a student's mode of study - the maximum allowance in terms remains the same for full- and part-time students.

source_title: Policy on Leave of Absence (intermission) for Postgraduate Research Degree students
question: A PGR student sponsored on a Student visa wants to intermit for two terms. What are the consequences?
expected_answer: The University is required to withdraw sponsorship from a student who intermits, and the Home Office will curtail their immigration permission. The student will have to leave the UK while intermitting, and must stop any work immediately because the condition allowing work alongside study no longer applies. Before returning they can request further immigration sponsorship and, if eligible, apply for a new Student visa. Retrospective intermission is not possible for sponsored students.
follow_up_question: While they are registered, are there rules about how their supervision meetings must be held because they are visa-sponsored?
follow_up_expected_answer: Yes. For students with immigration sponsorship the majority of contact should be face-to-face; in exceptional circumstances the University may agree contact via video link, and virtual meetings must not breach progress monitoring requirements for students subject to immigration control.
follow_up_keyphrases: majority of contact should be face-to-face

source_title: Policy on Thesis Submission, Deposit and Retention
question: Our student intends to submit their thesis at the end of their completion period. What do they need to do in advance, and how much notice is required?
expected_answer: They must give the Postgraduate Research Education Team at least three months' notice of their intention to submit, via the Approval of Title form, which the PGRE Team needs to begin appointing examiners. Submitting it late is likely to delay the examination process. A student entering a completion period does so on the understanding that the full thesis will be ready for submission by the end of that period.
follow_up_question: They still owe some fees - does that matter?
follow_up_expected_answer: Yes. All registration fees and debts must be paid before the thesis can be accepted for submission.
follow_up_keyphrases: before the thesis can be accepted

source_title: Code of Practice: Postgraduate Research Degrees
question: If the RSPB recommends a one-term extension to a student's standard period, how does that affect their completion time and their submission deadline?
expected_answer: The RSPB can recommend an extension of up to one term where milestone requirements for entering a completion period have not been met. The subsequent number of completion periods available is reduced by one term, unless exceptional circumstances make that reduction inappropriate, and the student must be offered the chance to discuss this with the RSPB before the recommendation goes to the Dean. For candidates first registered from October 2018 onwards the submission deadline is the end of the standard period of study, so extending that period moves the deadline.
keyphrases: end of the standard period of study
follow_up_question: Is the deadline the same for someone who registered before 2018?
follow_up_expected_answer: No. For candidates first registered before October 2018 the submission deadline of the thesis for examination is the end of the completion period, rather than the end of the standard period of study.

source_title: Policy on Leave of Absence (intermission) for Postgraduate Research Degree students
question: A first-year PGR student is asking for three terms of leave. Is that possible, and is there a shorter option?
expected_answer: It is possible but consequential: if a student requests a leave of absence during their first year of study which extends for longer than two terms, they will be required to restart the course. For short-term needs following bereavement or the serious illness of a close relative, compassionate leave of up to two weeks is a separate and lighter-touch option that automatically extends the study periods and submission date.
follow_up_question: If the reason is illness, how is that decided?
follow_up_expected_answer: Requests for intermission due to ill health are judged on a case-by-case basis. If the case is sound and backed by medical evidence, leave of absence is generally agreed regardless of the stage of the degree, with the length depending on the illness and its severity.

source_title: Policy for the Appointment of Independent Chairs for Research Degree Vivas
question: A thesis was referred and the student has now resubmitted. Do we need an Independent Chair for the second viva, and can the viva be waived?
expected_answer: Two separate rules apply. An Independent Chair is appointed where the viva follows a referral and resubmission of a thesis, so yes. On waiving, where the recommendation on the referred thesis is a pass, a request by the examiners to waive the viva will normally be granted; where the recommendation is not a pass, a waiver will only be granted in exceptional circumstances.
follow_up_question: Who can be the Independent Chair - can it be someone from the same department?
follow_up_expected_answer: No. The Independent Chair will be from outside the candidate's department and will have no conflict of interest with the candidate, the supervisor or the External Examiner. A nominee must be a permanent member of staff who has been an Internal Examiner for at least two postgraduate research examinations at Essex, or has examined two theses externally and undertaken University of Essex Independent Chair training.
follow_up_keyphrases: at least two postgraduate research examinations

source_title: Code of Practice: Professional Doctorates for the Tavistock and Portman NHS Foundation Trust 2025-26
question: A Tavistock professional doctorate student needs an extension to their standard period. Who recommends it and which Dean approves it?
expected_answer: The recommendation can only be made by the RSPB - a decision or recommendation to extend the standard period, like discontinuation, downgrading or permitting entry into completion, can only be made by the RSPB. For Tavistock and Portman programmes 'Dean' means the Dean of Partnerships (or their deputy), so approval is sought there rather than from the Executive Dean.
keyphrases: can only be made by the RSPB
follow_up_question: Is that a different route from an Essex-based professional doctorate?
follow_up_expected_answer: Yes in respect of the Dean and the reporting line. On Essex professional doctorates the Professional Doctorate Director is responsible to the Head of Department and most decisions are referred to the Faculty Dean Postgraduate; for the Trust programmes the Course Lead is responsible to the Portfolio Manager and decisions go to the Dean of Partnerships. The RSPB-only rule for these decisions is the same in both.

source_title: Code of Practice: Postgraduate Research Degrees
question: We want a visiting academic to supervise a research student. Could they instead act as Independent Chair at a viva?
expected_answer: Visiting staff cannot be appointed as a supervisor of a PGR student unless formally appointed via the associate supervisor route. Nor could they be an Independent Chair: a nominee must be a permanent member of staff who has been an Internal Examiner for at least two postgraduate research examinations at Essex, or has examined two theses externally and undertaken University of Essex Independent Chair training.
follow_up_question: If the supervisor is inexperienced, does that change who should chair the Supervisory Panel?
follow_up_expected_answer: Yes. Where the supervisor is a less experienced member of staff who has not supervised a student through to completion, the chair must be an experienced supervisor.
follow_up_keyphrases: chair must be an experienced supervisor

question: Our internal examiner has never examined a research degree before. What does that mean for how the viva is run?
expected_answer: An Independent Chair will be appointed: the Faculty Dean (Postgraduate) appoints one where the Internal Examiner has no experience in research degree examining, or is new to research degree examining at Essex and has not undertaken Internal Examiner training. The Independent Chair oversees the conduct of the oral examination. If the viva runs longer than two hours the internal examiner or Independent Chair will recommend an adjournment for a break.
keyphrases: no experience in research degree examining
follow_up_question: Can the supervisor sit in to support the inexperienced examiner?
follow_up_expected_answer: Not normally. The candidate's supervisor will not normally be present at the viva and can only be present in exceptional circumstances, approved on an individual basis by the Faculty Dean (Postgraduate) and with the agreement of the examiners. It is good practice for the supervisor to be invited in at the end when the examiners communicate their recommendation.

source_title: Policy on Thesis Submission, Deposit and Retention
question: How should a professional doctorate candidate submit their thesis, and what happens next in the examination process?
expected_answer: All candidates for Masters by Dissertation, MPhil, MD, PhD and Professional Doctorate must submit the thesis electronically in PDF format, contained within one document rather than separate files, emailed to the Postgraduate Research Team at pgrsubmission@essex.ac.uk, with all registration fees and debts paid first.
